optionReasons.dva-ini-003:option:0: The CloudFront distributes content by the edge and can stay NA FRENTE of a API, but does not create or manage routes, authorizations and integrations of API.
optionReasons.dva-ini-003:option:2: The Route 53 solve names DNS — does not create or manage APIs.
optionReasons.dva-ini-003:option:3: The CodeBuild compiles and tests code in CI pipelines — does not expose APIs.

finalJustifications: Because API Gateway creates and manages APIs REST and WebSocket with native integration to Lambda, caring for authentication, throttling and internships.
Because API Gateway hosts and executes function code Lambda in their own endpoints, eliminating the separate deployment of the function.
Because API Gateway is the only service capable of invoking a Lambda synchronous — the other triggers only work asynchronous.
Because API Gateway converts each route REST in a managed table, continuing the requests payloads automatically.

optionReasons.dva-ini-008:option:0: Bank NoSQL is the DynamoDB — Beantalk is an application deployment platform.
optionReasons.dva-ini-008:option:1: DNS managed is the Route 53 — nothing to do with application deployment.
optionReasons.dva-ini-008:option:2: Store Docker Images is the role of ECR; the Beanstalk even wheels containers, but it is a complete deployment platform, not a registry.

finalJustifications: Because Beanstalk is PaaS: you send the code and it provides EC2, ELB, Auto Scaling and monitoring automatically.
Because Beanstalk eliminates the collection of instances EC2 underlying — only the fixed fee of the managed platform is paid.
Because Beanstalk prevents direct access to the infrastructure provided, ensuring that no one manually alters resources.
Because Beanstalk compiles and packs Java applications automatically, the native runtime for which the platform was created.

optionReasons.dva-ini-010:option:0: The CodeArtifact stores PACOTES and dependencies (npm, pip, Maven) — not Git source repositories.
optionReasons.dva-ini-010:option:1: The CodeDeploy IMPLANTA applications in EC2, Lambda and ECS — does not store source code.
optionReasons.dva-ini-010:option:2: The CodePipeline orchestrate the flow of IC/CD between services — not repository.

finalJustifications: Because CodeCommit is Git's managed repository AWS: private, encrypted and with access controlled by IAM.
Because CodeCommit automatically compiles the code at each push, generating the build artifacts directly in the repository.
Because CodeCommit replaces Git's protocol with its own transport AWS, faster for large repositories.
Because CodeCommit versions templates and configuration files YAML used by account deployment pipelines.

optionReasons.dva-ini-009:option:0: The SES send transactional emails — nothing to do with infrastructure.
optionReasons.dva-ini-009:option:2: The CloudWatch MONITORA resources with metrics and alarms — does not define or provide.
optionReasons.dva-ini-009:option:3: X-Ray tracks distributed requests — is observability, not provisioning.

finalJustifications: Because CloudFormation Read Templates JSON/YAML declarative and provides resources as stacks — repeatable and with automatic rollback.
Because CloudFormation executes bash configuration scripts on the provided servers, applying the status described in the template.
Because CloudFormation monitor the infrastructure after creation, automatically correcting drift without team intervention.
Because CloudFormation generates the application code from the reporting template, unifying infrastructure and business logic.

optionReasons.dva-ini-028:option:1: The IAM manage identities of OPERADORES Account AWS — create a user IAM per app client is anti-standard and has no social login or registration flows.
optionReasons.dva-ini-028:option:2: Directory Service is Active Directory managed for Windows corporate scenarios — it is not directory of end-user application with social login.
optionReasons.dva-ini-028:option:3: Pure text passwords in a bank violate any security practice — and the team would have to build the entire backend.

finalJustifications: Because User Pool is the managed directory of end users: registration, email verification, password recovery and social federation ready, issuing tokens JWT.
Because User Pool delivers credentials AWS temporary for users to access S3 and DynamoDB directly — is that the role of the managed identity directory.
Because User Pool stores user passwords in a table of DynamoDB of your account, with hash and salt managed transparently by the service.
Because User Pool federates social login by also delegating the issue of the session to Google — the backend just needs to validate the password in local logins.

optionReasons.dva-ini-029:option:0: Save .tar from images in S3 even works as a deposit, but loses tags, image versioning, docker push/pull native, scanning and integration with ECS.
optionReasons.dva-ini-029:option:1: The EBS is storage of blocks for instances EC2 — not image log.
optionReasons.dva-ini-029:option:3: The CodeBuild CONSTROLE images in pipelines, but it is not the record that stores them and version.

finalJustifications: Because ECR is the managed image record: private repositories with push/pull docker, tags, vulnerability scan and permissions IAM.
Because ECR also runs stored containers: each push publishes the image and uploads the tasks directly to the cluster ECS integrated.
Because ECR converts Docker images to AMIs EC2, allowing the same artifact to revolve in instances and containers.
Because ECR compacts the layers of the images to the format accepted by Lambda, Unifying the Deployment of Functions and Containers.

optionReasons.dva-ini-002:option:0: The DynamoDB does not use XML — items are stored as attribute documents (view JSON).
optionReasons.dva-ini-002:option:2: Items DO NOT need to have the same attributes — each item may have different fields.
optionReasons.dva-ini-002:option:3: Set all columns before is the model RELACIONAL — no DynamoDB only the primary key is mandatory in the schema.

finalJustifications: Why not DynamoDB only the primary key is fixed in the schema — each item can load different attributes (schemaless).
Because DynamoDB validates the types of all attributes in the table creation, ensuring consistency of schema between the items.
Because DynamoDB automatically migrates the schema when a new item arrives with attributes different from those already stored.
Because DynamoDB stores items as rows of a table SQL Distributed, with fixed columns defined by the partition key.

optionReasons.dva-ini-013:option:1: Logs are generated by the execution and go to the CloudWatch — the handler is what RECEBE the invocation, not the log.
optionReasons.dva-ini-013:option:2: Network Configuration of the Lambda is in the settings of VPC function — not in the handler.
optionReasons.dva-ini-013:option:3: No web server to install — the Lambda is serverless; runtime invokes its code directly.

finalJustifications: Because the handler is the input point configured in the function: at each invocation the service calls it passing the event and the context.
Because the handler defines the maximum execution time of the function — the timeout is read from the method signature to each invocation.
Because the handler is executed only in the first invocation (cold start), initializing the runtime that answers the following calls.
Because the handler rotates the traffic HTTP for the correct port of the built-in server that runtime of Lambda starts by default.
